result.title: Do VLMs Really Look at the Road? A Diagnostic Evaluation for Autonomous Driving
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly being evaluated for autonomous driving through question-answering benchmarks, yet high benchmark accuracy does not necessarily reflect visually grounded reasoning. We present a diagnostic evaluation framework that systematically probes whether VLMs base safety-critical driving decisions on visual evidence or instead rely on language priors, answer biases, and dataset regularities. Our benchmark comprises two task categories, Adverse Weather and Junctions \& Intersections, with a nuScenes spatial reasoning extension, and evaluates open-source (general, driving, and spatial-reasoning) VLMs along four diagnostic protocols: image versus no-image evaluation, counterfactual weather sensitivity, linguistic robustness under paraphrasing and negation, and spatial reasoning. All ground-truth labels are derived programmatically from BDD100K and DriveLM annotations, enabling reproducible evaluation without manual labeling. Across all models, we find that competitive overall accuracy conceals systematic failure modes, including strong affirmation bias, limited sensitivity to counterfactual scene changes, near-chance performance on negated questions despite high paraphrase consistency, and confident driving decisions even without visual input. These results demonstrate that current open-source VLMs remain insufficiently grounded for safety-critical autonomous driving and underscore the need for diagnostic evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 提出面向自动驾驶的诊断式评测框架，基于 BDD100K 与 DriveLM 标注构建恶劣天气、交叉路口及 nuScenes 空间推理任务，用「有图/无图对比、反事实天气敏感度、改写与否定鲁棒性、空间推理」四类协议检验开源 VLM 的安全决策是否真正依赖视觉证据。
AI.relevance_reason: 「有图/无图」与反事实敏感度直接对应视觉旁路和信息坍缩的诊断思路，可作为核查 VLM 是否使用视觉内容的证据来源；但论文未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成与更新，其否定条件下近乎随机的表现可供思考证据筛选与语言先验的相对贡献。
